observations.text: SP demonstrated the knowledge expected for this training unit, answering the questions on the daily assignment at the pre-flight briefing only after the IP developed the content of the exercise. The Flight Manual and the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual were used with assistance, and the IP had to indicate the paragraph before each limit was located. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent use of the handbooks required by BD 3-1/HATC is expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP answered the questions of the pre-flight briefing on the daily assignment after the IP's verbal cues, without the IP having to develop the content of the exercise. The takeoff minima of AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 were stated incorrectly at first and were corrected with delay once prompted, but the reference was located by SP in the publication. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP presented the exercises of the daily assignment with minor errors in the sequence of the briefed maneuvers, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The traffic pattern altitude and the reporting points were quoted from the MAIP without prompting, and the morning meteorological briefing was followed without difficulty. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knew in detail the exercises given as daily assignment and answered the questions of the pre-flight and post-flight briefings accurately and without delay. The Flight Manual limits, the airport traffic procedures and the applicable AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 minima were quoted with confidence and without reference to notes. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, having studied the handbooks required by BD 3-1/HATC before the sortie, knew in detail every exercise of the daily assignment and used the Flight Manual, the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual and the MAIP with confidence at all three briefing phases. The aerodynamic explanation of the maneuvers flown was given theoretically and correctly at the post-flight briefing, and the hypoxia symptoms with the corresponding actions were described without assistance. Depth of knowledge was above the level expected at this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to study confined to personal notes instead of the handbooks required by BD 3-1/HATC, did not know the composition of the exercises given as daily assignment and could not state the entry parameters of two briefed maneuvers. The IP had to develop the content of the assignment before the briefing could be completed. Further study of the Flight Manual and of the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, could not explain the airport traffic procedures of the alternate airfield when they were requested at the pre-flight briefing. The IP had to direct the reference to the MAIP and to supply the pattern entry and the reporting points. The item was not completed without assistance.

SP demonstrated the knowledge desired for the Training Section, answering the questions on the daily assignment and on the Flight Manual limits after the IP's verbal cues. Two values of the takeoff data were stated incorrectly and were corrected with delay once the publication was indicated, and no question was left unanswered after prompting. Marginal performance for the Training Section - recall from the handbooks without cues is expected in the following sorties.

SP presented the exercises of the daily assignment with minor errors in the maneuver parameters, recognized and corrected in a timely manner by reference to the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual and without IP's intervention. The meteorological principles discussed at the morning briefing were interpreted correctly and applied to the planning of the sortie. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knew in detail the exercises given as daily assignment and used the Flight Manual, the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual and the aeronautical publications with confidence at the pre-flight, in-flight and post-flight phases. The questions on the airport traffic procedures and on the planning of the flight were answered accurately and without delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, having prepared from the handbooks required by BD 3-1/HATC, knew every exercise of the daily assignment in detail and quoted the applicable Flight Manual limits and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 minima without reference to notes. The aerodynamic behavior of the aircraft in the stall series was explained theoretically at the post-flight briefing, and the sea and land survival procedures with the recovery signals from SAR means were described without assistance. Accuracy and completeness of the answers were above the level expected at this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to preparation restricted to the maneuvers flown in the previous sortie, did not know the exercises given as daily assignment for this unit and could not state the airspeed and the altitude block required for the new maneuvers. The IP had to develop the profile and supply the parameters before the briefing could be completed. The item was not completed without assistance and re-study of the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP, due to planning conducted without the current publication for the airfield in use, did not know the traffic pattern altitude and the reporting points that had been amended in the MAIP. The IP had to supply the current data and to direct the re-planning of the recovery. The item was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to memorization of the limits without reference to the tables of the Flight Manual, stated two operating limits incorrectly at the pre-flight briefing and did not relate them to the configuration briefed for the sortie. The correct values were reached only after the IP's verbal cues, with recognition and correction delayed to the post-flight briefing.

SP, due to lack of awareness of a published restriction that was available in the briefing material, did not identify the weather minima applicable to the planned recovery and continued the planning on the forecast alone. The restriction was acknowledged only after the IP's verbal prompt and the plan was corrected with delay at the end of the briefing. Knowledge of AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 and of the meteorological principles required at the morning briefing is to be reinforced.

SP demonstrated the knowledge required within the desired standards, answering the questions of all three briefing phases; however, two errors in the recall of the Flight Manual limits were corrected by SP without IP's intervention. The exercises of the daily assignment were known and the aeronautical publications were used correctly, but the answers on flight physiology were reached slowly. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed and confidence in the use of the handbooks are expected to improve.

SP knew in detail all exercises given as daily assignment and used the Flight Manual, the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual, AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 and the aeronautical publications with confidence and without prompting. The airport traffic procedures were described accurately and the flight was planned without the IP having to supply any element. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, having prepared from the handbooks required by BD 3-1/HATC, knew every exercise of the daily assignment in detail and answered the questions of the pre-flight, in-flight and post-flight phases accurately and without delay. The aerodynamic causes of the deviations observed in the maneuvers were explained theoretically at the post-flight briefing, and the effects of the profile flown on flight physiology were interpreted correctly. Knowledge of the aeronautical publications and of the survival and SAR procedures was above the level expected at this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to study of the daily assignment conducted from the syllabus headings and not from the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual, could not describe the execution of two briefed maneuvers and could not state their entry parameters or their completion criteria. The IP had to teach the sequence at the pre-flight briefing and to direct the execution of the maneuvers in flight. The item was not completed without assistance and the assignment is to be re-studied before the next sortie.

SP, due to incomplete knowledge of the limits applicable to the maneuver, did not know the airspeed and load factor limits published in the Flight Manual for the aerobatic sequence and could not decide whether the profile as briefed was permissible. The IP had to supply the limits and to direct the reconstruction of the profile before the sortie. The item was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to reliance on recall alone instead of a structured reference to the publications, did not answer the questions on the airport traffic procedures and on the flight planning data at the pre-flight briefing. The answers were reached only after the IP's verbal cues, and the incorrect pattern altitude was recognized and corrected with delay at the post-flight briefing.

SP, due to reliance on how the maneuver is habitually flown rather than on the published criteria, described the recovery of the exercise in the terms of the previous sortie and did not state the criteria of the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual. The published criteria were quoted only after the IP's verbal prompts and the difference was recognized with delay at the post-flight briefing. Use of the handbooks required by BD 3-1/HATC in the preparation of the daily assignment is to be re-established.

SP, due to preparation that covered the maneuver parameters but not the meteorological content of the assignment, gave an incorrect interpretation of the forecast icing level at the pre-flight briefing. The error was minor and was recognized and corrected by SP in a timely manner by reference to the data of the morning meteorological briefing, without IP's intervention. All remaining questions on the daily assignment and on the Flight Manual were answered accurately.

SP, due to a mistake in applying the correct procedure to the wrong condition, quoted the actions for a rapid decompression when the question concerned the recognition of hypoxia symptoms in an unpressurized cockpit. The error was identified and corrected by SP within the same answer, without IP's intervention, and the remaining questions on air medicine and flight physiology were answered accurately. The knowledge of the handbooks required by BD 3-1/HATC was not otherwise affected.

SP demonstrated the knowledge desired for this training unit, knowing the exercises of the daily assignment and using the Flight Manual and the aeronautical publications without IP's intervention. The answers on aerodynamics and on the sea and land survival procedures were correct but were given slowly, and two of them were completed only after SP had located the reference in the publication. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed of recall is expected to improve while the present accuracy is maintained.

SP knew in detail all exercises given as daily assignment and used the Flight Manual, the A/C Techniques and Procedures Manual, AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 and the aeronautical publications with confidence at the pre-flight briefing, in flight and at the post-flight briefing. The meteorological principles of the morning briefing were interpreted without difficulty and the aerodynamic behavior of the aircraft during the maneuvers was explained theoretically and correctly. The sea and land survival procedures and the recovery procedures from SAR means were described completely and without assistance. Above end of block MIF achieved.
